skill.name: routemux-models
skill.description: Look up which models a RouteMux API key can actually call, what they cost, their context window, and which capabilities and protocols they support. Use when the user asks which models are available, how much a model costs, which model to pick for a task, whether a model supports vision/images/video, or says 有哪些模型/这个模型多少钱/用哪个模型好/支持什么协议. Requires the ROUTEMUX_API_KEY environment variable.
skill.summary: Query the live RouteMux catalogue to compare available models, pricing, context limits, and capabilities.
skill.author: rootfily-ai

security_audit.summary: All 20 static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md. Markdown caused the shell hits, while the network and environment references support the documented request without evidence of exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The skill documents an authenticated request that sends ROUTEMUX_API_KEY to the RouteMux API.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the destination restricted to the documented RouteMux host, use TLS, and never print, persist, or include the key in model output.

remediation.issue: Shell command examples can be copied into a user environment.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a documented HTTP client or SDK when available, and explain that users should review commands before running them.

remediation.issue: The catalogue is live and can change between requests.
remediation.suggestion: Use the current response for every answer, state when a field is absent, and avoid caching credentials or stale prices.

content.value_statement: Choosing a model without current availability, pricing, or capability data can cause failed requests and poor tradeoffs. This skill queries the live RouteMux catalogue for the models your key can call.
actual_capabilities: Queries the live RouteMux model catalogue for the current API key.
Reports canonical model identifiers returned by the catalogue.
Reports prices and context windows when the response includes those fields.
Filters models by capability, modality, provider, supported parameter, or name.
Compares two or three returned models using price, context, latency, or modality when available.
limitations: The skill requires a valid ROUTEMUX_API_KEY environment variable.
It reports catalogue data and does not independently test model quality.
It cannot provide prices or capabilities that the live response omits.
Availability and capability flags can change after each request.

use_cases.title: Compare Available Models
use_cases.description: Inspect the live models available to a specific key before selecting an API route.

use_cases.title: Choose a Model for a Task
use_cases.description: Compare two or three returned models by price, context, latency, and modality when those fields are available.

use_cases.title: Verify Modality Support
use_cases.description: Check whether the current catalogue lists image input, video output, or another requested capability.

prompt_templates.title: List My Available Models
prompt_templates.prompt: List the models available to my RouteMux key. Include canonical ids, prices, context windows, and listed capabilities. Use only the live response.

prompt_templates.title: Filter by Capability
prompt_templates.prompt: Find models for image input. Show the canonical id and every relevant field returned by the catalogue. State when a field is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two or three models for this task: [describe task]. Use only returned fields, and explain the tradeoffs across price, context, latency, and modality when available.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate an Unsupported Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate why this request is unavailable: [capability or model]. Query the relevant filters, separate missing catalogue data from unsupported capability, and cite the returned evidence.

output_examples.input: Can this key call a model that accepts images?
output_examples.output: The live catalogue returned models with image input: [canonical ids from the current response]. Support was checked from the catalogue response.

output_examples.input: Which option should I use for a long technical document?
output_examples.output: The catalogue lists these candidates with the largest context windows: [current model ids]. Compare their returned prices and latency before choosing.
The current catalogue lists [model id] at [returned price]. If no price field was returned, the catalogue does not expose a price for this model.

best_practices: Query the live catalogue before making availability or pricing claims.
Use the canonical model id exactly as returned.
State clearly when the response omits a requested field.
anti_patterns: Do not answer from remembered model lists or stale documentation.
Do not invent prices, context windows, or capability flags.
Do not write the API key to files, logs, or user-facing output.

faq.question: What does this skill query?
faq.answer: It queries the RouteMux models catalogue for the models available to the current API key.

faq.question: Does it show every RouteMux model?
faq.answer: It shows models that the current key can call, which may be a restricted subset of the global catalogue.

faq.question: Can it recommend a model?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare two or three returned models using fields such as price, context, latency, and modality.

faq.question: Can it verify image or video support?
faq.answer: Yes. It can filter by listed input or output modality and report the returned capability data.

faq.question: What happens when pricing is missing?
faq.answer: It reports that the catalogue does not expose a price instead of guessing.

faq.question: How is the API key handled?
faq.answer: The skill expects ROUTEMUX_API_KEY in the environment and instructs users not to write or disclose it.
